properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js provides SHA-256/SHA-512/RIPEMD160 that ethers.js uses for BIP32 HD-node derivation and Ethereum address computation; ships in the client bundle with ethers.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The secp256k1 ECDSA stack behind ethers.js@5, which this React NFT marketplace (Polygon/Goerli, MetaMask via window.ethereum) uses for every wallet transaction and account key. Changeable only by the Ethereum protocol itself — observable here, replaceable by the chain ecosystem.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The OpenSSL EVP_BytesToKey password KDF (single-round MD5) as implemented by the real npm package evp_bytestokey@^1.0.0/^1.0.3 — a genuine transitive dependency of browserify-aes and browserify-cipher inside crypto-browserify@3.12.0. config-overrides.js wires crypto-browserify into the production client bundle ("crypto": require.resolve("crypto-browserify")), so this weak KDF ships in the app artifact. No direct call site in the application source (app code only calls ethers/MetaMask); presence

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: bcrypt-pbkdf@^1.0.0 — Joyent's bcrypt-derived PBKDF (a KDF built on the bcrypt EksBlowfish core, distinct from the bcrypt password-hash function itself). Transitive dependency of sshpk (OpenSSH key parsing in the request/http stack of the hardhat toolchain). It also drags nested tweetnacl@0.14.5. Real declared dependency; dev toolchain only; no call site in application source.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge@1.3.1 provides RSA keygen/encrypt/sign among its primitives. Reached via selfsigned@2.0.1, which webpack-dev-server (react-scripts) uses to generate the dev HTTPS certificate. Quantum-relevant (RSA key transport) but dev-toolchain-only here: no RSA call site in application source; the algorithms ship with the dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: create-ecdh@4.0.0 is the ECDH implementation of the crypto-browserify browser polyfill (Node crypto shim over elliptic: secp256k1, secp256r1 via curves, curve25519). config-overrides.js:5 explicitly aliases "crypto" to crypto-browserify for the client bundle, so this ECDH capability ships in the production web artifact even though the application code never calls createECDH directly. Changeable here (remove the polyfill wiring if unused).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@0.14.5 (the instance nested under bcrypt-pbkdf in the sshpk chain) implements Ed25519 signatures (nacl.sign.detached). Available in the shipped dependency tree (dev toolchain via sshpk's OpenSSH key parsing); no call site in application source. Shor-vulnerable signature scheme; migration ML-DSA-65 if this path ever becomes production code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic is the ECDSA-over-secp256k1 engine ethers.js uses for Ethereum account keys and transaction signatures — bundled into the browser app. Shor-vulnerable signature primitive.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@0.14.5 implements X25519 scalar multiplication (nacl.scalarMult) — classical DH, retroactively breakable. Available in the shipped dependency tree via the sshpk/bcrypt-pbkdf dev chain; no call site in application source. Migration X25519MLKEM768 hybrid if this path ever becomes production code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 via @ethersproject/keccak256@5.6.1 and other Keccak consumers in the ethers/hardhat dependency trees. Keccak-256 is Ethereum's canonical hash (transaction hashing, address derivation, ABI encoding) — bundled into the client with ethers.js. Not quantum-urgent (Grover square-root only).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2 is the KDF ethers.js offers for encrypting JSON keystore wallets (kdf=pbkdf2 alongside scrypt); the plain pbkdf2 package also ships in the client bundle via the crypto-browserify polyfill wired at config-overrides.js:5.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js@3.0.1 is the memory-hard KDF that ethers@5.6.8 (declared devDependency, used by hardhat scripts) uses to decrypt Ethereum V3 keystore JSON wallets (scrypt N=131072, r=8, p=1). scrypt itself is a strong password KDF and not quantum-vulnerable; the asset records that wallet-key derivation happens with these parameters when ethers keystores are used. No direct scrypt call in application source.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge@1.3.1 provides AES (CBC/CTR/GCM) among its primitives, reached via selfsigned@2.0.1 in the react-scripts/webpack-dev-server dev chain. Symmetric AE — not quantum-vulnerable at current key sizes. Available in the shipped dependency tree; no AES call site in application source.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@0.14.5's secretbox (XSalsa20-Poly1305): authenticated symmetric encryption — not quantum-vulnerable (hence the A+ rating). Available in the shipped dependency tree via the sshpk/bcrypt-pbkdf dev chain; no call site in application source. Presence is the inventory fact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The tweetnacl crypto library ships in this project's dependency tree at two versions: top-level tweetnacl@1.0.3 (dev, pulled by sshpk for OpenSSH key parsing in the request stack) and tweetnacl@0.14.5 nested under bcrypt-pbkdf. Provides Ed25519, X25519, XSalsa20-Poly1305, SHA-512. No application call site; the library's presence is the inventory fact (it is what a bundle could reach). Changeable here only by pruning the dev dependency chain.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge@1.3.1 is a genuine crypto library in the dependency tree: required by selfsigned@2.0.1, which webpack-dev-server (via react-scripts) uses to generate the dev HTTPS certificate. Provides RSA, AES, X.509, PKCS#7/12, TLS, HMAC, PRNG. Dev-toolchain chain only — the production client bundle does not import it (the client polyfill is crypto-browserify); no application call site. Availability is the inventory fact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: selfsigned@2.0.1 generates the self-signed X.509 certificate that webpack-dev-server uses to serve the dev app over HTTPS. No certificates are committed to the repo (verified: no .crt/.pem/PEM blocks) — the cert is generated at dev time with node-forge. Dev-only posture: fine for local development, must never be trusted in production. Observable here, changeable via react-scripts dev-server HTTPS configuration.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge@1.3.1's X.509 machinery (certificate creation/parsing, CSR, PKCS#12), reached via selfsigned@2.0.1 in the react-scripts dev chain for the webpack-dev-server HTTPS certificate. Dev-toolchain only; no X.509 handling in application source and no committed certificates in the repo.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js is the scrypt KDF behind @ethersproject/wallet — the memory-hard KDF ethers.js uses to encrypt/decrypt JSON keystore wallets. Ships in the client bundle via ethers.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha.js (pure-JS SHA-1/SHA-224/256/384/512) is a dependency of crypto-browserify, which config-overrides.js:5 wires into the production client bundle as the 'crypto' fallback — this is the Node-crypto hash surface (createHash) that ships to browsers.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.5.4 — the secp256k1 ECDSA implementation behind ethers.js signing; bundled into the browser app with ethers. Shor-vulnerable; migration means Ethereum protocol/account-abstraction changes, not a library swap.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: selfsigned generates the self-signed X.509 certificate for Hardhat's local HTTPS JSON-RPC endpoint — development/test tooling only, never shipped to the browser bundle.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js@1.1.7 — SHA-256/SHA-512/RIPEMD160 for BIP32 HD-wallet derivation and Ethereum address hashing inside ethers.js; ships in the client bundle.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The npm pbkdf2 package: dependency of crypto-browserify (client polyfill per config-overrides.js:5) and the PBKDF2 implementation used by @ethersproject/wallet for keystore encryption. Same PBKDF2 usage family as ALG-4de3b020, which aggregates the pbkdf2-named entries.
